work.title: CASE STORY
work.subtitle: A permission-aware narrative feature
work.scope: An authored fictional scenario about a workshop handover. Not a real customer case, interview, testimonial, permission record or measured improvement.

pages.title: Name the story’s status first.
pages.lead: A clearer handover begins with a question. In this fictional workshop story, a maker wants the next person to understand why a production note matters.
pages.body: Use the narrative to explore a communication problem, not to imply a customer endorsement. The characters and sequence are authored examples, and no interview or publication permission has been obtained.
pages.detail: An actual case study needs a defined scope, participant agreement and review process. Illustration does not provide likeness or testimonial rights.
pages.question: Would a reader mistake this story for a real customer account?

records.label: Story status
records.prompt: Authored fictional scenario; no actual customer.

records.label: Permission status
records.prompt: Not obtained; no real participant approached.

records.label: Publication boundary
records.prompt: Do not present the narrative as a testimonial.

evidenceRows: No participant permission or measured change supplied.

pages.title: Set a scene without a success claim.
pages.lead: A small ceramics workshop prepares materials for the next shift. A note lists the objects to finish, but does not explain why one batch needs special attention.
pages.body: The scene establishes a task and a missing piece of context. It does not establish the frequency of this problem, the size of the workshop or the financial cost of a misunderstanding.
pages.detail: Describe only the details needed to understand the decision. In a real case, check the setting and operational details with the relevant participant.
pages.question: Which contextual detail explains the task rather than decorating it?

records.label: Setting
records.prompt: Fictional ceramics workshop between shifts.

records.label: Task
records.prompt: Explain a batch-specific decision to the next maker.

records.label: Missing context
records.prompt: Why this batch needs a different review.

evidenceRows: No participant permission or measured change supplied.

pages.title: Make the challenge observable.
pages.lead: The next maker can read what to do but cannot see the reasoning behind the instruction. The challenge is continuity of understanding, not a proven productivity loss.
pages.body: A real story would need evidence of the original practice and its limitations. Avoid manufacturing a dramatic before-state simply to make the proposed change appear effective.
pages.detail: The note separates instruction from explanation. That is the fictional tension; claims about delays, mistakes or savings are not supplied.
pages.question: What observation would support the challenge in an actual workshop?

records.label: Before-state
records.prompt: Instruction exists without its original rationale.

records.label: Consequence question
records.prompt: Can the next maker interpret the exception?

records.label: Evidence gap
records.prompt: No observation or error record supplied.

evidenceRows: No participant permission or measured change supplied.

pages.title: Explain the choice and alternatives.
pages.lead: The maker chooses to add a short context card beside the batch note. Another option would be a conversation or a clearer annotation on the original sheet.
pages.body: The choice is modest and reversible. It is not a claim that one product outperforms all alternatives. A credible case acknowledges what was considered and why the selected approach fit the immediate task.
pages.detail: Keep the rationale separate from an outcome. A plausible reason for trying something does not prove that the trial worked.
pages.question: Could a simpler alternative address the same need?

records.label: Chosen approach
records.prompt: Add a short explanation beside the instruction.

records.label: Alternative
records.prompt: Clarify the existing sheet or speak directly.

records.label: Selection reason
records.prompt: Keep the rationale available at the handover.

evidenceRows: No participant permission or measured change supplied.

pages.title: Show the action in sequence.
pages.lead: The maker writes the batch reference, the reason for the exception and the question the next shift should check before continuing.
pages.body: A second person reads the card and identifies what remains unclear. This is the authored action sequence, not an observed adoption process or a record of staff training.
pages.detail: The card does not replace specialist judgement or operational safety instructions. In an actual setting, confirm how the note fits authorised procedures.
pages.question: Where would the receiving person ask for clarification?

records.label: Step one
records.prompt: Link the instruction to the relevant batch.

records.label: Step two
records.prompt: Explain the reason for the exception.

records.label: Step three
records.prompt: Leave an explicit question for the next reviewer.

evidenceRows: No participant permission or measured change supplied.

pages.title: Describe change without making up a result.
pages.lead: The proposed after-state is a handover note that carries both instruction and rationale. Whether that changes understanding or work quality remains an open question.
pages.body: No before-and-after measurement, time saving or customer quotation exists in this example. A real outcome section should identify its source, timeframe and uncertainty instead of substituting a persuasive number.
pages.detail: Use the phrase proposed after-state until an appropriate observation exists. The narrative structure is complete even when a real-world result is unknown.
pages.question: What source would support a change in understanding?

records.label: Proposed change
records.prompt: Instruction and rationale appear together.

records.label: Measured result
records.prompt: Not supplied; no before-and-after comparison.

records.label: Quote status
records.prompt: No participant quotation or endorsement supplied.

evidenceRows: No participant permission or measured change supplied.

pages.title: Keep a source trail for every assertion.
pages.lead: A publishable case lets a reviewer distinguish direct observation, participant interpretation and the writer’s summary. This fictional story contains only authored narrative.
pages.body: The five-item source register marks setting, challenge, action, outcome and quotation boundaries. It is not an interview transcript or a record of participant approval.
pages.detail: For a real case, retain reviewable notes and the permitted scope of use. Do not treat a polished sentence as evidence merely because it sounds specific.
pages.question: Can each assertion be traced to an appropriate source?

records.label: Observation
records.prompt: None supplied for this authored scenario.

records.label: Interpretation
records.prompt: Writer’s illustrative explanation, not participant testimony.

records.label: Approval
records.prompt: No actual source or participant review completed.

evidenceRows: No participant permission or measured change supplied.

pages.title: Give limitations space in the story.
pages.lead: A context card may help only when the next person can find it, interpret it and act within the relevant procedure. The card itself guarantees none of those conditions.
pages.body: The example does not generalise to other workshops or tasks. An actual case should describe dependencies and alternative explanations rather than turning one account into a universal benefit.
pages.detail: Permission, accessibility, workflow fit and operational responsibility need separate checks. A narrative cannot settle them by implication.
pages.question: Which condition could make the proposed approach unsuitable?

records.label: Dependency
records.prompt: The receiving person can find and interpret the note.

records.label: Alternative explanation
records.prompt: A clearer original instruction may be sufficient.

records.label: Generalisation
records.prompt: No broader effectiveness claim established.

evidenceRows: No participant permission or measured change supplied.

pages.title: Extract a useful lesson, not an endorsement.
pages.lead: The lesson is to keep an instruction close to its reason and to leave room for the next person’s question. That is an editorial principle, not a customer result.
pages.body: If adapting a real case, distinguish a paraphrase from a quotation and agree the permitted attribution. Do not place invented words inside quotation marks or attach them to a real person.
pages.detail: Try this review question: what would the next person need to understand before using this note? It invites inquiry without claiming a guaranteed outcome.
pages.question: Does the takeaway remain honest without the story’s fictional setting?

records.label: Lesson
records.prompt: Keep the reason near the instruction.

records.label: Attribution
records.prompt: No actual speaker or participant endorsement.

records.label: Reuse boundary
records.prompt: Check quotation and attribution permissions separately.

evidenceRows: No participant permission or measured change supplied.

pages.title: Close with a relevant conversation.
pages.lead: If your handovers lose context, start by examining one note with the people who use it. Ask what information is missing before choosing a new tool.
pages.body: This is an invitation to consider a task, not an offer of a functioning service. A real contact destination should explain what the reader can expect and how any shared information will be used.
pages.subheading: Next step with a clear boundary
pages.detail: Review the story status and permissions again before sharing. Retain the distinction between an illustrative case and evidence from an actual organisation.
pages.question: What is the smallest appropriate next conversation?

records.label: Reader action
records.prompt: Review one handover note with its intended reader.

records.label: Contact status
records.prompt: No live contact service or response promise supplied.

records.label: Sharing check
records.prompt: Keep fictional status and source limits visible.

evidenceRows: No participant permission or measured change supplied.
